sections.title: Dual-Framework (Compatibility Bridge)
sections.content:
Python GUI code is traditionally tightly coupled to either PyQt6 or PySide6. VenvHub Pro resolves this via an automated Compatibility Bridge (core/logic/pyqt_to_pyside.py) implementing a low-level MetaPathFinder hook.

  • On main.py launch, runtime framework discovery triggers.
  • If PyQt6 is detected, the app executes natively.
  • If PySide6 is present, the bridge intercepts all from PyQt6... import statements in memory and redirects them seamlessly to PySide6.
Outcome: The codebase is written 100% in clean PyQt6 syntax while dynamically executing on host PySide6 environments without code alterations.

sections.title: UI Template Virtualization (QUiLoader Mimic)
sections.content:
Frameworks load XML UI definitions differently:

  • PyQt6 (uic.loadUi): Mounts widgets directly into the existing window instance (self).
  • PySide6 (QUiLoader): Strictly spawns a new window instance.

VenvHub Pro integrates an intelligent Mimic Engine: Under PySide6, QUiLoader builds the XML graph, then programmatically extracts all child widgets and layouts, binding them onto the primary self instance with relative icon path preservation.

sections.title: Self-Replication Pipeline (Dogfooding)
sections.content:
Because VenvHub Pro includes a built-in PyInstaller Builder, the application compiles itself without external build scripts.

  1. Launch VenvHub Pro.
  2. Set the Projects Root to the VenvHub Pro source repository in Settings.
  3. Open PyInstaller Builder and select main.py as the entry point.
  4. Configure Assets and compilation parameters.
  5. Click BUILD .EXE.
Dogfooding validates the builder's reliability by successfully compiling its own complex codebase.

sections.title: PyInstaller Build Variants (PyQt6 vs PySide6)
sections.content:
Because PyInstaller relies on static AST inspection, compilation settings adapt based on the GUI runtime in your active Venv.

Required Assets:
Always bundle these core folders (source = destination): ui, core/themes, translations, assets, navod.

Branch A: Compiling with PyQt6

PyInstaller traces imports directly from main.py and bundles required PyQt6 binaries automatically. No extra flags are needed in the Imports tab.

Branch B: Compiling with PySide6

Because the source code references PyQt6, PyInstaller requires explicit directives in the Imports tab:

  • Hidden Imports: Append: PySide6, PySide6.QtCore, PySide6.QtGui, PySide6.QtWidgets, PySide6.QtNetwork, PySide6.QtUiTools.
  • Exclude Modules: Exclude PyQt6 to prevent redundant binary bloat.

At startup, the runtime Bridge initializes and links the bundled PySide6 framework seamlessly.

sections.title: Packaging Distributables with NSIS
sections.content:
Regardless of the build branch, compiling in directory mode (--onedir) generates dist/VenvHubPro.

To generate an enterprise installer using NSIS, package the output directory:

# NSIS Script directive:
File /r "path\to\project\dist\VenvHubPro\*"

NSIS compresses the bundle (LZMA) into a standalone Setup.exe installer with desktop shortcut generation.
